title: Judges Chapter 21 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Judges chapter 21 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Judges Chapter 21 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Judges Chapter 21.

questions.question: What oath did the men of Israel swear in Mizpeh concerning the tribe of Benjamin?
options: They would not give their daughters to Benjamin to wife
They would fight alongside Benjamin
They would give their daughters to Benjamin to wife
They would exile Benjamin
questions.correctAnswer: They would not give their daughters to Benjamin to wife
questions.explanation: Judges 21:1 states that the men of Israel had sworn in Mizpeh that none of them would give his daughter unto Benjamin to wife.

questions.question: Where did the people of Israel go and stay till evening while weeping sore?
options: The house of God
The city gates
The fields of Jabeshgilead
The rock Rimmon
questions.correctAnswer: The house of God
questions.explanation: Judges 21:2 explains that the people came to the house of God, stayed there till evening, lifted up their voices, and wept sore.

questions.question: What question did the Israelites ask the LORD God of Israel in their prayer?
options: Why is there one tribe lacking in Israel today?
Why have we lost the battle?
Why did Benjamin rebel against us?
Why did the LORD forsake us?
questions.correctAnswer: Why is there one tribe lacking in Israel today?
questions.explanation: Judges 21:3 records the people asking God why there should be one tribe lacking in Israel that day.

questions.question: What did the people do early the next day after their prayer?
options: Built an altar and offered burnt and peace offerings
Went to war against Benjamin
Sent messengers to Jabeshgilead
Searched for wives for Benjamin
questions.correctAnswer: Built an altar and offered burnt and peace offerings
questions.explanation: Judges 21:4 states that on the morrow the people rose early, built an altar, and offered burnt and peace offerings.

questions.question: According to Judges 21:5, what was the consequence for anyone who did not come up to the LORD at Mizpeh?
options: He shall surely be put to death
He will be banished
He will be forgiven
He will be given a wife from Benjamin
questions.correctAnswer: He shall surely be put to death
questions.explanation: Judges 21:5 says a great oath was made that whoever did not come up to the LORD at Mizpeh shall surely be put to death.

questions.question: True or False: The children of Israel repented for Benjamin their brother and lamented that one tribe was cut off from Israel.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Judges 21:6 states that the children of Israel repented for Benjamin, recognizing that one tribe was cut off from Israel that day.

questions.question: What problem did the Israelites face concerning the tribe of Benjamin after their oath?
options: How to find wives for the remaining Benjaminites
How to wage war against Benjamin
How to rebuild Benjamin's cities
How to divide land among tribes
questions.correctAnswer: How to find wives for the remaining Benjaminites
questions.explanation: Judges 21:7 shows the Israelites wondering how to provide wives for Benjamin since they had sworn not to give their daughters to them.

questions.question: Which tribe's inhabitants did not come up to Mizpeh to the LORD, as discovered by the Israelites?
options: Jabeshgilead
Benjamin
Ephraim
Judah
questions.correctAnswer: Jabeshgilead
questions.explanation: Judges 21:8 states that none came to the camp from Jabeshgilead to the assembly at Mizpeh.

questions.question: True or False: When the people numbered the inhabitants, they found many from Jabeshgilead present at Mizpeh.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Judges 21:9 explains that when the people were numbered, none of the inhabitants of Jabeshgilead were found there.

questions.question: What was the first action taken by the congregation against Jabeshgilead?
options: Sent twelve thousand valiant men to smite them with the sword
Offered peace treaties
Built an altar in Jabeshgilead
Called Jabeshgilead to the assembly
questions.correctAnswer: Sent twelve thousand valiant men to smite them with the sword
questions.explanation: Judges 21:10 says the congregation sent twelve thousand men to smite the inhabitants of Jabeshgilead with the edge of the sword.

questions.question: True or False: The Israelites were commanded to utterly destroy every male and every woman who had lain by man in Jabeshgilead.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Judges 21:11 commands that every male and every woman who had lain by man be utterly destroyed in Jabeshgilead.

questions.question: How many young virgins were found among the inhabitants of Jabeshgilead who had not known a man?
options: Four hundred
One thousand
Two hundred
Three hundred
questions.correctAnswer: Four hundred
questions.explanation: Judges 21:12 states that four hundred young virgins who had not known a man were found among the inhabitants of Jabeshgilead.

questions.question: Where did the Israelites bring the four hundred virgins from Jabeshgilead?
options: To the camp at Shiloh
To Mizpeh
To the rock Rimmon
To Bethel
questions.correctAnswer: To the camp at Shiloh
questions.explanation: Judges 21:12 also says they brought the virgins to the camp at Shiloh, which is in the land of Canaan.

questions.question: In Judges 21, which event happened first?
options: The men of Israel swore not to give daughters to Benjamin
The Israelites attacked Jabeshgilead
The children of Benjamin took wives from Shiloh
The people built an altar and offered sacrifices
questions.correctAnswer: The men of Israel swore not to give daughters to Benjamin
questions.explanation: Judges 21:1 shows the oath sworn at Mizpeh came before the altar building (v.4), the attack on Jabeshgilead (v.10), and the taking of wives from Shiloh (v.23).

questions.question: True or False: The people of Israel wept and lifted up their voices before God because one tribe was missing from Israel.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Judges 21:2-3 describes the people weeping before God and asking why one tribe was lacking in Israel.

medium.title: Judges Chapter 21 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Judges Chapter 21 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What command did the congregation give to the twelve thousand valiant men sent to Jabeshgilead?
options: Go and smite the inhabitants with the edge of the sword, including women and children
Capture the inhabitants and bring them to Shiloh for judgment
Make peace with the inhabitants and invite them to join Israel
Take only the men as prisoners and leave the women and children unharmed
questions.correctAnswer: Go and smite the inhabitants with the edge of the sword, including women and children
questions.explanation: Judges 21:10 clearly states that the twelve thousand men were commanded to go and smite the inhabitants of Jabeshgilead with the edge of the sword, including women and children. This is reiterated with instructions to utterly destroy every male and every woman who had lain with a man in Judges 21:11.

questions.question: According to Judges 21:11, what specific instruction was given regarding the women of Jabeshgilead?
options: Utterly destroy every male and every woman that had lain with a man
Take all women as wives for the tribe of Benjamin
Keep the women as captives for labor
Allow the women to return to their families unharmed
questions.correctAnswer: Utterly destroy every male and every woman that had lain with a man
questions.explanation: Verse 11 directs the men to destroy every male and every woman who had known a man sexually. This shows the severity of the judgment against Jabeshgilead’s inhabitants as part of the effort to provide wives for Benjamin while maintaining the oath integrity.

questions.question: How many young virgins did the men find among the inhabitants of Jabeshgilead, and what was done with them?
options: Four hundred young virgins were found and brought to Shiloh to be wives for Benjamin
Two hundred young virgins were found and sent back to their families
Five hundred young virgins were taken as captives for other tribes
No virgins were found; all women were destroyed
questions.correctAnswer: Four hundred young virgins were found and brought to Shiloh to be wives for Benjamin
questions.explanation: Judges 21:12 states that four hundred young virgins who had not lain with a man were found and brought to the camp at Shiloh to provide wives for the remaining Benjaminite men, highlighting the attempt to preserve the tribe.

questions.question: What action did the congregation take to communicate with the children of Benjamin in the rock Rimmon?
options: Sent messengers to speak peaceably and call them to come back
Launched a surprise attack to capture them
Ignored them and let them stay isolated
Sent provisions but no message
questions.correctAnswer: Sent messengers to speak peaceably and call them to come back
questions.explanation: Judges 21:13 notes that the congregation sent some to speak peaceably to the children of Benjamin in the rock Rimmon, calling them to return. This shows the desire for reconciliation and restoration despite the prior conflict.

questions.question: What was the result after Benjamin received the wives from Jabeshgilead?
options: They had wives but still not enough to satisfy them
They rejected the women and went back to war
They divided the women among all tribes equally
They sent the women back to Jabeshgilead
questions.correctAnswer: They had wives but still not enough to satisfy them
questions.explanation: Verse 14 reveals that Benjamin received wives from Jabeshgilead but these were still insufficient to meet the needs of the remaining men, indicating the ongoing challenge of sustaining the tribe.

questions.question: Why did the people repent for Benjamin according to Judges 21:15?
options: Because the LORD had made a breach in the tribes of Israel
Because Benjamin had defeated the other tribes
Because Benjamin refused to fight
Because Benjamin was the strongest tribe
questions.correctAnswer: Because the LORD had made a breach in the tribes of Israel
questions.explanation: Judges 21:15 states that the people repented for Benjamin because the LORD had made a breach in the tribes of Israel. This shows their recognition of divine judgment and the need for restoration and unity.

questions.question: What concern did the elders express about finding wives for the remaining Benjamites?
options: The women of Benjamin had been destroyed, making it difficult to find wives
They feared the women would refuse to marry Benjamin
They wanted to give daughters from other tribes instead
They planned to adopt wives from neighboring nations
questions.correctAnswer: The women of Benjamin had been destroyed, making it difficult to find wives
questions.explanation: Judges 21:16 highlights the elders’ concern that the women in Benjamin were destroyed, so they questioned how to find wives for the remaining men, underscoring the crisis facing the tribe.

questions.question: What did the Israelites decide about the inheritance and survival of the tribe of Benjamin?
options: There must be an inheritance for those who escaped so the tribe isn't destroyed
Benjamin should be divided among other tribes
Benjamin should be excluded from Israel permanently
Benjamin should be given land outside Israel
questions.correctAnswer: There must be an inheritance for those who escaped so the tribe isn't destroyed
questions.explanation: Judges 21:17 explains that the Israelites decided to ensure an inheritance for the survivors of Benjamin to prevent a tribe from being wiped out, reflecting a concern for tribal continuity and God's covenant people.

questions.question: Why did the Israelites say they could not give their daughters as wives to Benjamin?
options: Because they had sworn an oath saying cursed be he that giveth a wife to Benjamin
Because their daughters refused to marry Benjamin
Because Benjamin did not want their daughters
Because the daughters were reserved for priests
questions.correctAnswer: Because they had sworn an oath saying cursed be he that giveth a wife to Benjamin
questions.explanation: Judges 21:18 states that the Israelites had made a solemn oath that cursed anyone who gave a wife to Benjamin, creating a major obstacle to providing wives from their own daughters.

questions.question: What annual event did the Israelites identify as an opportunity to find wives for Benjamin?
options: A feast of the LORD in Shiloh
A harvest festival in Bethel
A war games gathering in Shechem
A market day in Lebonah
questions.correctAnswer: A feast of the LORD in Shiloh
questions.explanation: Judges 21:19 describes a yearly feast of the LORD in Shiloh that took place near Bethel on the highway to Shechem, which they planned to use as an opportunity to find wives for Benjamin.

questions.question: What strategy did the Israelites command Benjamin to use during the feast to acquire wives?
options: Lie in wait in the vineyards and catch the daughters of Shiloh as they danced
Ask the fathers of the daughters for their consent
Trade livestock for wives in the market
Invite the daughters to the Benjaminite camp for a feast
questions.correctAnswer: Lie in wait in the vineyards and catch the daughters of Shiloh as they danced
questions.explanation: Judges 21:20-21 instruct Benjamin to lie in wait in the vineyards and catch each man a wife from the daughters of Shiloh as they came out to dance, a plan made to circumvent the oath and provide wives.

questions.question: What reason did the Israelites give to the fathers and brothers of the daughters they took as wives?
options: They asked to be favorable because the daughters were not given to Benjamin in the war
They promised to pay a bride price
They said the daughters chose to leave willingly
They threatened to go to war if complaints were made
questions.correctAnswer: They asked to be favorable because the daughters were not given to Benjamin in the war
questions.explanation: Judges 21:22 explains that if the fathers or brothers complained, the Israelites would say to be favorable because they had not given their daughters to Benjamin during the time of war, so they were not guilty.

questions.question: What did the children of Benjamin do after taking the wives from the daughters of Shiloh?
options: They returned to their inheritance, repaired the cities, and dwelt in them
They went to war against other tribes
They sent the wives back to their families
They abandoned their cities and became nomads
questions.correctAnswer: They returned to their inheritance, repaired the cities, and dwelt in them
questions.explanation: Verse 23 states that Benjamin took wives, returned to their inheritance, repaired cities, and dwelt in them, showing restoration and rebuilding of the tribe.

questions.question: What does Judges 21:24 say about the Israelites after these events?
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Judges 21:24 says that the children of Israel departed at that time, every man to his tribe and family, returning to his inheritance. This shows a return to order and tribal identity after the crisis.

questions.question: Does Judges 21:25 imply that during this time, Israel had a king who ruled over them?
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Judges 21:25 explicitly states there was no king in Israel during those days and that every man did what was right in his own eyes, indicating a lack of centralized leadership.

hard.title: Judges Chapter 21 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Judges Chapter 21.

questions.question: Where was the yearly feast of the LORD held, as mentioned in Judges 21?
options: Shiloh
Bethel
Shechem
Lebonah
questions.correctAnswer: Shiloh
questions.explanation: Judges 21:19 states that the feast of the LORD was held yearly in Shiloh.

questions.question: What instruction was given to the children of Benjamin regarding the daughters of Shiloh?
options: Lie in wait in the vineyards and catch wives from the daughters of Shiloh
Ask the daughters of Shiloh for wives openly
Send gifts to the fathers of the daughters of Shiloh
Marry daughters only from their own tribe
questions.correctAnswer: Lie in wait in the vineyards and catch wives from the daughters of Shiloh
questions.explanation: Judges 21:20-21 commands the children of Benjamin to lie in wait in the vineyards and catch wives from the daughters of Shiloh when they come out to dance.

questions.question: What reason did the Israelites give to the fathers or brethren of the daughters of Shiloh if they complained about the daughters being taken as wives?
options: They reserved not to each man his wife in the war
They paid a bride price
They sought God's permission
They promised compensation later
questions.correctAnswer: They reserved not to each man his wife in the war
questions.explanation: Judges 21:22 explains that the Israelites would say they did not reserve wives for Benjamin during the war, so they should be treated favorably.

questions.question: After receiving wives from the daughters of Shiloh, what did the children of Benjamin do according to Judges 21?
options: Returned to their inheritance, repaired the cities, and dwelt in them
Built a new city named after their wives
Went to Bethel to celebrate
Moved to the land of Canaan
questions.correctAnswer: Returned to their inheritance, repaired the cities, and dwelt in them
questions.explanation: Judges 21:23 records that the children of Benjamin took wives, returned to their inheritance, repaired their cities, and dwelt there.

questions.question: What does Judges 21:25 reveal about leadership in Israel during this period?
options: There was no king in Israel; every man did what was right in his own eyes
Israel was ruled by a high priest
A single king ruled all tribes
Judges were appointed to lead
questions.correctAnswer: There was no king in Israel; every man did what was right in his own eyes
questions.explanation: Judges 21:25 states there was no king, and everyone acted according to their own judgment.

questions.question: Which tribe was cut off from Israel prompting the need to find wives for its remaining men?
options: Benjamin
Judah
Ephraim
Levi
questions.correctAnswer: Benjamin
questions.explanation: Judges 21:6 mentions that Benjamin was the tribe cut off from Israel, leading to concern for their survival.

questions.question: What was the oath the men of Israel swore at Mizpeh about giving daughters to Benjamin?
options: They would not give any of their daughters to Benjamin as wives
They would only give daughters to Benjamin if approved by the elders
They would give daughters only if Benjamin repented
They would give daughters to Benjamin willingly
questions.correctAnswer: They would not give any of their daughters to Benjamin as wives
questions.explanation: Judges 21:1 states the men of Israel swore that none would give their daughters to Benjamin as wives.

questions.question: From which city did the Israelites take four hundred young virgins for the Benjamites?
options: Jabeshgilead
Rimmon
Shiloh
Bethlehem
questions.correctAnswer: Jabeshgilead
questions.explanation: Judges 21:12 reveals that four hundred young virgins were taken from Jabeshgilead for the Benjamites.

questions.question: Which literary device is evident in the narrative of Judges 21 where the Israelites both cut off and then preserve the tribe of Benjamin?
options: Inclusio
Simile
Allegory
Hyperbole
questions.correctAnswer: Inclusio
questions.explanation: The chapter begins and ends with the concern about the survival of Benjamin, framing the narrative—a classic example of inclusio (Judges 21:1 and 21:17).

questions.question: What Hebrew word meaning is significant in understanding the term 'breach' used in Judges 21:15 regarding the tribes of Israel?
options: A break or rupture in unity
A military fortress
A covenant agreement
A joyful celebration
questions.correctAnswer: A break or rupture in unity
questions.explanation: 'Breach' in Judges 21:15 signifies a break or rupture in the unity of Israel, emphasizing the division caused among the tribes.

questions.question: How does the situation in Judges 21 echo the concerns found in Deuteronomy 7 regarding inter-tribal marriages?
options: Both warn about marrying outside the tribe or covenant community
Both encourage marrying from foreign nations
Both promote polygamy to increase population
Neither addresses marriage issues
questions.correctAnswer: Both warn about marrying outside the tribe or covenant community
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 7 warns against marrying outside the covenant community to avoid idolatry, echoing the concern in Judges 21 about controlling Israelite marriages (Judges 21:7 and Deuteronomy 7:3).

questions.question: What does the action of the Israelites taking wives by force in Judges 21 foreshadow in biblical history?
options: The complexities and moral challenges in Israel's leadership and covenant obedience
The establishment of a monarchy in Israel
The construction of the Temple in Jerusalem
The Exodus from Egypt
questions.correctAnswer: The complexities and moral challenges in Israel's leadership and covenant obedience
questions.explanation: The forced taking of wives reflects the chaotic moral state in Israel, foreshadowing the need for centralized leadership and covenant faithfulness (Judges 21:25).

questions.question: True or False: The Israelites repented for Benjamin because the LORD had made a breach in the tribes of Israel.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Judges 21:15 explicitly states that the people repented for Benjamin because the LORD had made a breach in Israel's tribes.

questions.question: True or False: According to Judges 21, the Israelites gave their daughters willingly as wives to the Benjamites after the oath at Mizpeh.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Judges 21:1 and 21:18 show that Israelites had sworn not to give their daughters to Benjamin, and the wives were taken by other means, not willingly given.

questions.question: Which other Old Testament book contains a similar theme of lamenting the loss or near destruction of a tribe as found in Judges 21?
options: 1 Samuel
Exodus
Leviticus
Nehemiah
questions.correctAnswer: 1 Samuel
questions.explanation: In 1 Samuel 14, there is concern for the tribe of Benjamin’s survival, echoing Judges 21's theme of preserving the tribe.

theological.title: Judges Chapter 21 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Judges Chapter 21 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What solemn action did the men of Israel take at Mizpeh concerning the tribe of Benjamin?
options: They swore not to give their daughters to Benjamin to wife
They declared Benjamin their king
They offered Benjamin their best livestock
They invited Benjamin to lead the tribes
questions.correctAnswer: They swore not to give their daughters to Benjamin to wife
questions.explanation: Judges 21:1 shows that the men of Israel made a solemn oath at Mizpeh that no one would give his daughter to a man of Benjamin as a wife, indicating the tribe's isolation.

questions.question: How does Judges 21:2 demonstrate the human response to corporate sin and calamity?
options: The people prayed and wept before God until evening
The people rebelled against God
The people ignored the problem
The people offered sacrifices without repentance
questions.correctAnswer: The people prayed and wept before God until evening
questions.explanation: Judges 21:2 reveals the people’s heartfelt repentance and mourning before God, reflecting a biblical pattern of contrition in response to national sin.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is implicitly revealed in the Israelites' lament about a tribe being 'lacking' in Israel (Judges 21:3)?
options: God’s justice in preserving the unity of His people
God’s wrath against idolatry
God’s patience with sinners
God’s sovereignty over nature
questions.correctAnswer: God’s justice in preserving the unity of His people
questions.explanation: Judges 21:3 shows concern over a tribe being cut off, reflecting God's just governance which demands the preservation of Israel's unity as His covenant people.

questions.question: What theological implication arises from the people building an altar and offering burnt and peace offerings after their lament (Judges 21:4)?
options: God’s provision of atonement through sacrifice
God’s acceptance of human works alone
God’s indifference to sin
God’s rejection of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: God’s provision of atonement through sacrifice
questions.explanation: Judges 21:4 demonstrates the necessity of sacrifice to express repentance and seek peace with God, pointing to the broader biblical doctrine of atonement.

questions.question: What doctrine is highlighted by the Israelites' question in Judges 21:7 about providing wives for Benjamin despite their oath?
options: The tension between covenant vows and mercy
The permanence of human oaths over God’s commands
The rejection of inter-tribal relationships
The impossibility of repentance
questions.correctAnswer: The tension between covenant vows and mercy
questions.explanation: Judges 21:7 reflects the complex issue of upholding solemn oaths while addressing the need for mercy and restoration within the covenant community.

questions.question: What does the command to utterly destroy all males and any woman who had lain with a man in Jabeshgilead (Judges 21:11) reveal about Israel’s understanding of holiness?
options: The demand for ritual purity and covenant faithfulness
A disregard for human life
An endorsement of indiscriminate violence
A purely political strategy
questions.correctAnswer: The demand for ritual purity and covenant faithfulness
questions.explanation: Judges 21:11 shows the severe measures Israel took to maintain holiness and purity by removing those who broke covenant norms, reflecting the seriousness of sin in the community.

questions.question: How does the rescue of four hundred virgins from Jabeshgilead (Judges 21:12) illustrate God's providential preservation of a remnant?
options: It shows God’s mercy in preserving a future for Benjamin
It indicates human ingenuity without divine involvement
It reveals a failure of the tribes to act justly
It highlights the extinction of Benjamin
questions.correctAnswer: It shows God’s mercy in preserving a future for Benjamin
questions.explanation: Judges 21:12 reveals God's providential care in preserving virgins to provide wives for Benjamin, sustaining the tribe and pointing to the biblical theme of a preserved remnant.

questions.question: What redemptive narrative connection is made by the children of Israel sending to call peaceably to Benjamin in the rock of Rimmon (Judges 21:13)?
options: The restoration of a fragmented people foreshadowing the unity in Christ
The establishment of a new covenant with Benjamin
The rejection of Benjamin from Israel
The rise of a new monarchy
questions.correctAnswer: The restoration of a fragmented people foreshadowing the unity in Christ
questions.explanation: Judges 21:13 illustrates efforts to reconcile and restore unity among Israel's tribes, echoing the biblical trajectory toward ultimate reconciliation through Christ.

questions.question: Combining Judges 21:14 and 21:15, what doctrinal insight emerges about human repentance and divine judgment?
options: Human repentance follows divine chastening and acknowledges God’s sovereign discipline
Repentance can prevent all judgment
Divine judgment is arbitrary and unrelenting
Human actions have no impact on divine decisions
questions.correctAnswer: Human repentance follows divine chastening and acknowledges God’s sovereign discipline
questions.explanation: Verses 21:14-15 show Israel’s repentance prompted by the breach God made among the tribes, teaching that repentance is a response to God’s righteous discipline.

questions.question: What does the elders’ concern in Judges 21:16 about the destruction of Benjamin highlight about God’s covenant promises?
options: The importance of preserving each tribe as part of God’s covenant people
The dispensability of tribal identity
The supremacy of personal ambition
The end of God’s promises to Israel
questions.correctAnswer: The importance of preserving each tribe as part of God’s covenant people
questions.explanation: Judges 21:16 reflects the theological concern to maintain tribal continuity, which is vital for the fulfillment of God's covenant promises to Israel.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that Judges 21 condones immoral actions such as stealing women. What does Judges 21:20-23 actually teach regarding the people’s actions?
options: It reveals a pragmatic but tragic attempt to preserve the tribe of Benjamin within covenantal boundaries
It endorses lawless and corrupt behavior
It promotes idol worship
It instructs complete anarchy
questions.correctAnswer: It reveals a pragmatic but tragic attempt to preserve the tribe of Benjamin within covenantal boundaries
questions.explanation: Judges 21:20-23 shows the Israelites’ desperate measures to preserve Benjamin, reflecting human fallenness and the tragic consequences of broken oaths, not divine approval of immorality.

questions.question: How does Judges 21:25 reveal the spiritual condition of Israel during this period?
options: There was no king, and everyone did what was right in their own eyes
Israel was united under a righteous king
The priests ruled over Israel with divine authority
The people followed the law strictly
questions.correctAnswer: There was no king, and everyone did what was right in their own eyes
questions.explanation: Judges 21:25 highlights the lack of centralized godly authority, resulting in moral relativism and societal chaos, illustrating the need for righteous leadership.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is most evident in the Israelites’ repentance and building of an altar after their lament (Judges 21:4)?
options: God’s mercy and readiness to forgive
God’s indifference to human actions
God’s wrath without relief
God’s silence in judgment
questions.correctAnswer: God’s mercy and readiness to forgive
questions.explanation: Judges 21:4 shows God’s mercy as the people respond to Him in repentance with offerings, indicating that He is willing to forgive upon sincere repentance.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal teaching emerges from Judges 21:6 and Judges 21:18 about Israel’s oath and its consequences?
options: Oaths made before God have binding consequences that can lead to unintended hardship, requiring wisdom and mercy
Oaths are easily broken without consequence
Oaths are irrelevant to covenant relationships
Oaths alone can save a tribe
questions.correctAnswer: Oaths made before God have binding consequences that can lead to unintended hardship, requiring wisdom and mercy
questions.explanation: Judges 21:6 and 21:18 together show that the oath not to give wives to Benjamin caused a crisis, emphasizing the seriousness of vows and the need to balance justice with mercy.

questions.question: What narrative significance does the yearly feast at Shiloh mentioned in Judges 21:19 have in Israel’s worship history?
options: It represents a central place of worship and covenant renewal before the monarchy
It was a pagan festival adopted by Israel
It was a minor event with no spiritual significance
It marks the establishment of the temple in Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: It represents a central place of worship and covenant renewal before the monarchy
questions.explanation: Judges 21:19 points to Shiloh as a key cultic center where Israel gathered yearly, illustrating the continuation of covenant worship in the period before the temple and monarchy.
